claims.text: Wear performance in CuMoTaWV protective coatings is primarily governed by the residual stress state induced during deposition.
Compressive residual stress enhances the hardness of CuMoTaWV coatings.
Compressive residual stress delays crack initiation in CuMoTaWV coatings.
Tensile residual stress accelerates wear by promoting early crack formation and delamination.
Baseline sputtering conditions produce as-deposited CuMoTaWV films with near-neutral residual stress.
Changing sputter power and deposition rate can produce controlled compressive or tensile residual-stress states in CuMoTaWV coatings.
The relevant structural mediator is the magnitude and sign of residual stress in the as-deposited coating.
Residual stress in the coating can be characterized using XRD or TEM-based techniques.
Compressive residual stress increases resistance to near-surface plastic deformation during sliding wear.
Tensile residual stress makes CuMoTaWV coatings more prone to microcracking and delamination.
Greater compressive residual stress will produce lower wear rates than near-neutral or tensile residual stress under otherwise identical wear conditions.
Greater compressive residual stress will produce lower friction coefficients than near-neutral or tensile residual stress.
The predicted residual-stress dependence of wear and friction will hold at room temperature.
The predicted residual-stress dependence of wear and friction will hold at approximately 300 °C.
Residual stress is expected to remain the dominant wear mechanism in CuMoTaWV films up to approximately 300 °C.
At higher temperatures or under substantially different wear regimes, mechanisms other than residual stress may significantly affect wear.
Changing deposition parameters may alter microstructural features in addition to residual stress, making the residual-stress effect difficult to isolate.

Failure of compressively stressed coatings to show consistently lower wear and friction, or failure to observe a relationship between residual stress and cracking, would falsify the proposed governing role of residual stress.
